claims.claim_text: Capital One completed its acquisition of Discover Financial Services on May 18, 2025, and Discover's businesses constituted approximately 21% of total assets and 20% of total net revenues as of/for the year ended December 31, 2025.
claims.source_quote: As permitted by the SEC, management's assessment of and conclusion on the effectiveness of the Company's internal control over financial reporting as of December 31, 2025, did not include the internal controls of Discover, which was acquired by the Company on May 18, 2025. Discover's businesses constituted approximately 21% of total assets and 20% of total net revenues as of and for the year ended December 31, 2025.
claims.subject: Discover Financial Services

source_params.search_term: Capital One Discover merger closing May 18 2025

claims.extraction_notes: Discover deal closing is a hard, registry-verifiable event: Capital One/Discover 8-K filings, Federal Reserve approval orders, and CFR Board orders all leave a documented trail. EDGAR fulltext should yield merger-closing 8-K filings at or near 2025-05-18.

claims.claim_text: On January 22, 2026, Capital One entered into an Agreement and Plan of Merger to acquire Brex Inc. for $5.15 billion in aggregate consideration (~$2.58B cash plus approximately 10.6 million COF shares).
claims.source_quote: On January 22, 2026, Capital One Financial Corporation entered into an Agreement and Plan of Merger and Reorganization (the Brex Merger Agreement ) with Brex Inc., a Delaware corporation ( Brex ), and certain other parties thereto, pursuant to which, upon the terms and subject to the conditions set forth therein, the Company will acquire Brex (the Brex Transaction ). The completion of the Brex Transaction is subject to the satisfaction of customary closing conditions, including clearance under the Hart-Scott-Rodino Antitrust Improvements Act of 1976, as amended. Pursuant to the terms and subject to the conditions set forth in the Brex Merger Agreement, the Company will acquire the outstanding equity of Brex for $ 5.15 billion in aggregate consideration, subject to certain adjustments described in the Brex Merger Agreement, consisting of approximately $ 2.58 billion in cash and approximately 10.6 million shares of common stock of Capital One.
claims.subject: Brex Inc.
claims.extraction_notes: Brex is a private company, so its own SEC trail is limited; however COF will have filed an 8-K Item 1.01 referencing the Brex Merger Agreement on/about 2026-01-22. EDGAR fulltext restricted to COF's CIK will adjudicate the existence and terms of the agreement. HSR clearance can additionally be tracked via the FTC Early Termination Notices registry (separate connector would be needed for HSR adjudication).

claims.claim_text: Capital One relies on Amazon Web Services for cloud infrastructure, on Total System Services LLC (TSYS) for North American and U.K. consumer/commercial credit-card processing, and on Fidelity Information Services (FIS) for certain banking systems.
claims.source_quote: These relationships include, but are not limited to: Amazon Web Services, Inc. ( AWS ) for our cloud infrastructure, Total System Services LLC ( TSYS ) for consumer and commercial credit card processing services for our North American and U.K. portfolios and Fidelity Information Services ( FIS ) for certain of our banking systems.
claims.subject: AWS / TSYS / FIS
claims.extraction_notes: Layer 3 Rule 7: a multi-year cloud-and-processing relationship of Capital One's scale should be material enough for AMZN/AWS, Global Payments (TSYS parent), and FIS to reference Capital One in their own 10-Ks as a major customer (or in the case of TSYS/Global Payments, in segment/customer-concentration disclosures). EDGAR fulltext run against AMZN's CIK for 'Capital One' is a weak test (named customers are rarely listed in AMZN 10-K) but TSYS/Global Payments customer concentration is the meaningful read. Likely UNVERIFIABLE for AMZN; weakly verifiable for Global Payments.

claims.claim_text: As of December 31, 2025, Capital One's senior unsecured long-term debt is rated Baa1 by Moody's, BBB by S&P, and A- by Fitch (with CONA at A3 / BBB+ / A respectively).
claims.source_quote: Table 31: Senior Unsecured Long-Term Debt Credit Ratings December 31, 2025 December 31, 2024 Capital One Financial Corporation CONA Capital One Financial Corporation CONA Moody s Baa1 A3 Baa1 A3 S&P BBB BBB+ BBB BBB+ Fitch A- A A- A As of February 13, 2026, Moody s Investors Service ( Moody s ) and Fitch Ratings ( Fitch ) have our credit ratings on a stable outlook and Standard & Poor s ( S&P ) has our credit ratings on a positive outlook.
claims.subject: Capital One Financial Corporation senior unsecured debt
claims.object_value: Moody's Baa1 / S&P BBB / Fitch A-
claims.extraction_notes: Credit ratings are proprietary opinions of three private NRSROs (Moody's, S&P, Fitch). No free public registry adjudicates ratings as of a date; the rating agencies' own websites are paywalled or registration-gated and not authoritatively redistributable. Could in principle be cross-checked via the issuer's bond prospectus filings on EDGAR but the rating itself remains proprietary. Marked NONE rather than build a fragile scraper.

claims.claim_text: As of December 31, 2025, Capital One had $729.6 billion of total unfunded lending commitments (credit-card lines, loan commitments, letters of credit) versus $458.1 billion at December 31, 2024.
claims.source_quote: As of December 31, 2025 and 2024, our total unfunded lending commitments were $729.6 billion an d $458.1 billion, respectively, consisting of credit card lines, loan commitments to customers of both our Commercial Banking and Consumer Banking businesses, as well as standby and commercial letters of credit.
claims.subject: Capital One total unfunded lending commitments
claims.extraction_notes: FDIC Call Report Schedule RC-L (Off-Balance Sheet Items) reports unused commitments for credit card lines and other loan commitments at the bank-subsidiary level (CONA). Reported 10-K consolidated unfunded commitments should reconcile (with some HoldCo-level adjustments) to the sum across CONA + Discover Bank Call Reports for Q4 2025. Step-change from $458B to $729.6B is largely the Discover Card consolidation; Discover Bank's standalone Call Reports for Q4 2024 (pre-merger) plus CONA Q4 2024 should bracket the prior-year base.

claims.claim_text: Capital One recorded a provision for credit losses of $20.655 billion in 2025, up 76% from $11.716 billion in 2024.
claims.subject: Capital One provision for credit losses
claims.extraction_notes: Calibration Heuristic note: 10-K provision is consolidated and includes the day-one CECL build for Discover's acquired portfolio (PCD + non-PCD allowance establishment), which inflates 2025 vs prior-year. The FDIC Call Reports for CONA + Discover Bank for FY2025 quarters should sum to a comparable figure net of HoldCo eliminations; the step-up vs FY2024 is real but the source of the step-up (acquisition accounting vs deteriorating credit) is a separable read. Lower-confidence emission unless the Phase 2 Scorer can decompose Discover Day-1 build.
